description: Compile-checked templates for FluentRoslyn. A meta-generator that runs on your source-generator project: mark a method [Template] and its body is real, compiled, refactorable C# that the meta-generator lifts into the FluentRoslyn calls which reproduce it. Breaking a template is an error in your own build, not a CS8785 warning in your consumer's.
releaseNotes:
0.1.0-preview.8

No changes to this package, for the third release running. It is still identical to 0.1.0-preview.5, its only substantive release; it shares a version line with FluentRoslyn, which does have changes here. No changes to this package, for the second release running. It is identical to 0.1.0-preview.5, which was its first and so far only substantive release; it shares a version line with FluentRoslyn, which does have a change in this release.

0.1.0-preview.6

No changes to this package. It is identical to 0.1.0-preview.5 and there is no reason to upgrade for its own sake; it shares a version line with FluentRoslyn, which does have changes in this release.

0.1.0-preview.5 — first release, alongside FluentRoslyn 0.1.0-preview.5.

Mark a method [Template] and its body becomes real, compiled, refactorable C#. The meta-generator reads your generator project's own syntax trees and lifts each template into the FluentRoslyn calls that reproduce it, so breaking a template is an error in your own build rather than a CS8785 warning in your consumer's — a warning that leaves the build green and the generated file silently missing.

Holes are marked in the template and filled at generation time. Diagnostics are reported under the FRT prefix.

The ceiling, stated rather than discovered later: a template is checked against the types your generator project can see. The consumer's types exist only when the generator runs, so anything a hole reaches into stays unchecked at that seam. "Type safe, almost" is the honest description.

Install into the source-generator project itself, not into the consumer.
